item.text:
**1B.2 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

Direct searches for AMLO nuclear rhetoric in 2024 found no credible evidence of reckless threats, brinkmanship, apocalyptic language, or normalization of nuclear use. The 2024 record I found is instead consistently disarmament-oriented and anti-escalation. One AMLO statement about the Middle East is relevant as broader anti-war rhetoric, though it is not nuclear-specific.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [“La política se inventó para evitar la guerra”, afirma presidente sobre conflicto en Medio Oriente](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/) | Presidente de México | 2024-04-13 | <https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/> | AMLO said politics exists to avoid war, urged that the Iran-Israel conflict not escalate, described war as irrational and harmful, and called for peace and fraternity. This is responsible anti-escalation rhetoric, though it is not directly nuclear-focused. | 1B.2 |
| [Mexico promotes peace at the eighth OPANAL course on nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-01-26 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en> | Mexico’s foreign ministry backed disarmament and non-proliferation training for officials from foreign affairs, defense, navy, and security. This supports a reading of institutional risk-reduction rather than reckless nuclear signaling. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| [Foreign Ministry prioritizes nuclear disarmament on Mexico’s international agenda](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en> | The foreign ministry framed Mexico’s diplomacy around a safer, more peaceful world grounded in international law and cooperation, at the Treaty of Tlatelolco anniversary. This is direct evidence of restrained, anti-nuclear rhetoric. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | <https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm> | Mexico’s representative urged fewer nuclear warheads, progress on disarmament, and less discourse threatening nuclear use, while rejecting the idea that nuclear weapons are part of the solution. This is the strongest 2024 direct evidence that the AMLO government used nuclear rhetoric responsibly. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported judgment: yes, the 2024 record shows responsible nuclear rhetoric.
- Strongest support comes from Mexico’s disarmament diplomacy and the UN First Committee statement.
- I found no reliable 2024 counterexample showing AMLO or his government using nuclear threats, brinkmanship, apocalyptic framing, or normalization of nuclear use.

**Search gap**

- I searched directly with multiple formulations for AMLO, Mexico, nuclear threats, and reckless rhetoric.
- The gap is specific: Mexico is not a nuclear-armed state, and I found no 2024 nuclear-brinkmanship episode to weigh against the disarmament statements.
- The only AMLO rhetoric I found that was remotely relevant was general anti-war language about the Middle East, not nuclear rhetoric.
